---
title: "Ragged Storage Append Semantics"
---

## Overview

`OwningRaggedStorage` (LineData, MaskData, PointData) and `OwningRaggedAnalogStorage`
store ragged entries in a contiguous Structure-of-Arrays (SoA) layout. Each
`TimeFrameIndex` maps to **one contiguous index block** in the parallel `_times`
array, enabling O(1) `getAtTime()` via `[start, end)` range lookup.

Implementation: `src/DataObjects/RaggedTimeSeries/include/RaggedTimeSeries/RaggedStorage.hpp`

## Append behavior

| Case | Complexity | Behavior |
|------|------------|----------|
| New time at tail | O(1) | `push_back` |
| Same time, consecutive tail | O(1) | Extend existing block |
| Revisit time after interleaving | O(n) | Insert at block end, shift tail |

Out-of-order append is **supported**. Callers always use `append` / `addAtTime`;
storage inserts at the end of the existing per-frame block when revisiting a
frame (e.g. label frame 50, then batch-write frames 1–100).

## Invariants

For every `(time, [start, end))` in `_time_ranges`:

- `start < end`
- `_times[i] == time` for all `i` in `[start, end)`

Debug builds call `validateTimeRanges()` after mutations to catch implementation
regressions.

## Legacy corrupted state

If in-memory data predating the insert-at-block-end fix has interleaved entries
(e.g. frame 50 at indices 0 and 50 with frames 1–49 between), `_rebuildAccelerationStructures`
detects invalid ranges and runs `_compactTimeBlocks()` (stable group-by-time)
before rebuilding maps.
